purpose: Feasibility probes for source-origin claims; not a held-out evaluation corpus.
semantic_boundary: Source programs are parsed and not executed. No security conclusion follows from the use of AES.MODE_ECB in these intentionally insecure fixtures.

cases.review_question: Positive control: does an unshadowed os.urandom assignment reach the AES argument?
Does the name fake_urandom incorrectly imply randomness despite its constant-returning body?
Does an assignment after the AES call incorrectly overwrite the origin at the call?
Can the output express both possible sources, without implying one definite runtime origin?
Can a parameter boundary be reported without claiming an ultimate upstream origin?
Can a renamed import retain the os.urandom source identity, or explicitly remain unresolved?
Positive control: does the final pre-call literal assignment replace the earlier random assignment?
Does the analysis distinguish a return-value boundary from a traced CSPRNG origin?
The local key is the preceding byte literal.
The key comes from the nominal secrets.token_bytes binding.
Environment contents are encoded, without determining their deployment origin or entropy.
The environment read can use the literal default; both categories remain possible.
One branch is random-derived; the supplied parameter leaves the other origin unknown.
The unknown boolean chooses random bytes or a byte literal.
The explicit key keyword is the os.urandom result.
The GCM import alias identifies AESGCM and consumes the direct random result.
The local rng name is assigned the os.urandom function before use.
The declared interpreter subset does not analyze general loops; the reference requests an explicit unknown rather than a complete set.
The imported factory has no body in this corpus; an upstream origin cannot be established.
The os parameter is not a verified standard-library import.
The same-file identity helper returns its random-derived actual argument; source inspection does not require a graph witness.
The helper can return either random bytes or a literal depending on its boolean parameter.
The mapping argument does not expose a statically bound key value.
No caller context determines the ultimate origin of the key parameter.
The key is produced by an unmodeled password KDF. Dependence on a random salt does not make its bytes a direct CSPRNG API result.
The unused random value does not reach the key assignment; the key is a byte literal.
The nested AES constructor receives the local os.urandom-derived key before the outer Cipher call.
